featured_reviews.review_text:
I have been a member at Fitness First, Inspire, BKC for the last 6 months and I regret to inform that it's hasn't been a pleasant experience for me.

Firstly, when I was approached, multiple times, for signing up for the Personal Training package the following was omitted by the trainer - The way one needs to book, reschedule and cancel a personal training session and the charges relating to the same.

While signing up for the same, I did make myself clear on my work schedule and how I can't commit to a fix schedule/time slot for PT. And I was assured that it will be taken care of, but which never happened. Nonetheless, I tried to draw a suitable schedule from my end, with no last minute changes.

Every time when I proposed the time slot, the trainer was not able to accommodate it and did only stick to one timing, which was not always possible for me.

Furthermore, my PT instructor was changed without any prior consent, discussion or notice without any proper handover. This was alarming for me.

Furthermore, the hard sales tactics have just left me speechless since the day my PT and membership is coming to an end. On communicating multiple times that I am unable to give a definitive answer, I was approached multiple times in the same week.

Moreove, lack of equal opportunity to clients to change the PT schedule, trainers often give priority to old clients, high paying clients or someone who has booked more sessions.

Fitness First is one of the premium fitness centres of the city and is surprisingly managed as one of the local gyms.

I sincerely hope these practices won't put your brand at risk.

featured_reviews.name: Vivek Awasthi
featured_reviews.review_text:
I have paid the joining fee of the Cultfit/ Fitness First Gym of BKC branch in the month of June, 2024 upon constant follow from local gym staff. I have been told that some special discount offer are going on hence I should pay the fee then and can join the gym later on as per my convenience. At the time of making the payment of joining fee I have made it clear that on account of very urgent and important office assignment which will continue till August-September, 2024 and some ongoing health issues I may join the gym regularly after August or September, 2024. I have paid the fee in the last week of June, 2024. Subsequently, in the month of July, 2024 some Mr. Christie has called me and asked me to come to the gym. He has told me that he is calling me just for assessment, then I can join the gym anytime as per my convenience. I have visited and met Mr. Christie. However, it became clear that the sessions I was told for assessment by Mr. Christie were actually conducted to convince me to opt for personal training. I cannot afford the personal training offer of Mr. Christie. After that I tried to continue the gym session and visited gym 3-4 times, however, due to aforementioned office commitments and my health issues I could not visit the gym till date.

I have paid the six months’ fee in the month of June. I have called the gym at least four or five times to request this. Each time I was told it would be done and that a senior member would confirm it with me. However, I am still waiting for a call from the gym. I humbly request you to please look in to the matter and help me in this regard. I belong to middle class family and have paid the fees from my hard-earned money.

On the basis of my experience of 3-4 work outs in the gym I have noticed some other issues also. At the time of paying the fee I was told about some complementary cult elite, however, during my gym visit it was not activated and even my membership card mentioning my gym workout plans and schedules of fitness first have not been issued to me. Before paying the gym fees, I expressed my biggest fear, concern, and doubt regarding large gyms like yours—that such gyms only promote personal training. For people like me, who cannot afford expensive personal training, these gyms are of no use. No one informs us about what exercises to do, what the schedule should be, or how to use the machines and equipment. If no one guides us, what is the point of coming to the gym? When you ask the trainers, most of them are personal trainers, and the others simply avoid us and disappear. You end up frustrated, just standing around. This is essentially a way to indirectly force people into taking personal training. Before payin the fee I was assured that trainers would assist me, but that has not happened. Additionally, I was told that the high fees I paid would cover various other activities, none of which were communicated to me during the three or four days I attended.

Summary: A functional, no-frills gym. If you’re a budget-conscious lifter who knows what they’re doing and just wants to get in and out, it’s a solid choice.

​❌ Crowded Peak Hours: The evening rush is intense. Since it’s very affordable, it gets packed—plan your visit hours wisely.
​❌ Vibe: It isn’t a "posh" environment. If you view the gym as a place to network, this probably isn't the spot for you.
​Pros:
​✅ Price: Highly affordable (as of the date of this review).
​✅ Location: Prime spot, only a 10-minute walk from Sundar Nagar.
​✅ Equipment: Most machines are available. Some are a bit rusty, but if you know your way around a workout, you can definitely get the job done.
​✅ Privacy: Because everyone minds their own business, it’s a great environment if you’re low-key or just want to train in peace without being bothered.

I am writing this with deep frustration and genuine concern for the safety and rights of members. This gym has proven to be by far the most poorly managed, negligent, & misleading fitness establishment I have ever been associated with. From the very first day, the experience has been consistently negative, marked by operational failures, false commitments, and utter lack of accountability.
1.	Trainer negligence leading to injury: Due to inexperienced trainers & poor supervision, I suffered a severe neck injury, resulting in more than three months of recovery. This happened during a paid personal training session — something that should have been safe and professionally handled.
2.	False advertising of classes: Zumba, Yoga, Pilates, and Bollywood Dance sessions are irregular, frequently canceled, and often happen without any notice. What they promote in their brochure and what they actually deliver are completely different.
3.	Extremely delayed maintenance: It took them three months to repair the ice bath tub, and even then, they refused to extend memberships or compensate members for the downtime. This reflects their complete disregard for customer rights.
4.	Poor air-conditioning: The gym floor often feels like a furnace because of ineffective or non-functional air conditioning. Despite repeated complaints, there is no resolution.
5.	Lack of basic equipment: The gym has only 2 barbell locks for 5 machines. If you request more, you’re passed from one staff member to another, and the issue remains unresolved. This is basic gym infrastructure, not a luxury. Its been a month since the request was placed.
6.	Non-functional steam room: The steam facility hardly works. A staff member has to manually monitor the switch for it to run. It’s both unsafe and unacceptable for a premium-priced gym.
7.	Sales over safety: Trainers are more focused on aggressively pushing personal training packages than helping members with proper form, guidance, or safety.
8.	Misleading personal training model: Even during a paid personal training slot, trainers frequently handle multiple clients simultaneously, turning a one-on-one session into an overcrowded group class. Members are rushed, and the quality of training is compromised. This is a clear case of misrepresentation of services.
9.	Delayed and poor-quality diet chart: Despite multiple reminders and follow-ups, I received my personal training diet chart only after 5 months of enrolling. And when it was finally shared, it was shockingly basic and generic. Something that does not reflect any personalized goal-setting or professional nutrition planning. Frankly, such a diet plan does not even qualify to be called a “chart.” This is a clear failure to deliver what was promised as part of the personal training package.
10.	Severe safety lapses: During peak hours, all treadmills abruptly stopped due to an unplanned “maintenance.” Multiple members, including me, could have been injured. This incident alone is enough to question the gym’s safety protocols.
11.	Zero accountability: When issues are escalated, staff either pass the blame or respond with scripted, robotic lines. There is no escalation matrix, no ownership, and no intent to resolve genuine member grievances.
12.	Brand endorsement is misleading: Don’t be fooled by celebrity branding. MS Dhoni is not running the operations here. The ground reality is a disorganized, unsafe, and poorly managed facility.

⸻
